artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \ge 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain. Given a finite set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, let $\mathrm{St}(S)$ denote the length (i.e., total Euclidean edge-length) of a minimum Steiner tree spanning $S$, that is, the infimum of the total length over all finite connected graphs embedded in $\mathbb{R}^d$ as a union of straight line segments and containing every point of $S$ as a vertex.

Fix a probabilistic model that produces, for each $N \ge 1$, a random set $X_N = \{X_1,\dots,X_N\} \subset \Omega$ of $N$ points (for instance, i.i.d. samples from a probability density $f$ on $\Omega$, or a point process of intensity proportional to $N$ restricted to $\Omega$).

Question: Does there exist a constant $\beta = \beta(\Omega, \text{model}, d) > 0$ such that
$$\lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{St}(X_N)}{N^{(d-1)/d}} = \beta,$$
and moreover such that $\mathrm{St}(X_N)/N^{(d-1)/d} \to \beta$ almost surely as $N \to \infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: The Steiner minimum tree length is a classical subadditive Euclidean functional, and Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley-type asymptotics of the form $\beta N^{(d-1)/d}$ are known for i.i.d. uniform samples in a bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (Steele, Yukich, and the general theory of subadditive/superadditive Euclidean functionals), with extensions to absolutely continuous distributions giving an explicit integral $\beta\int_\Omega f(x)^{(d-1)/d}dx$. However, BHH-type extensions are known to fail for general stationary ergodic inputs (counterexample by Arlotto–Steele), so the question phrased for an arbitrary "random model" is not fully resolved; the constants $\beta$ themselves are not known explicitly.

status_evidence.title: Probability and Problems in Euclidean Combinatorial Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: The Steiner minimal tree functional is among the classical subadditive Euclidean functionals to which BHH-type theorems apply, giving asymptotics of order N^{(d-1)/d} for i.i.d. points in [0,1]^d.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotics of order N^{(d-1)/d} are established for the Steiner tree length on i.i.d. uniform random points.

status_evidence.title: Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley theorem for stationary ergodic sequences: A counterexample (Arlotto–Steele)
status_evidence.snippet: BHH-type asymptotics do not extend from i.i.d. uniform inputs to general stationary ergodic sequences with uniform marginals.
status_evidence.claim: For general random models the BHH-type asymptotics can fail, so the question is not affirmatively answered for arbitrary random inputs.

status_evidence.title: Separating Subadditive Euclidean Functionals (Frieze–Pegden)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses constants β for various subadditive Euclidean functionals (TSP, MST, Steiner tree, matching) and shows they are distinct.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of the constants β for Steiner tree on uniform random points is part of the standard subadditive Euclidean functional framework, though their numerical values remain unknown.
